answer: A stake-bond registry resists Sybil attacks by requiring every agent identity to lock a refundable copper-token bond before it can transact. A new vertex in the trust graph gains weight only after its bond has aged unchallenged, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund each one separately and keep the funds locked. A bond caught cheating is slashed, pushing the attacker off the ledge of profitability: forging identities costs linearly while honest participants pay nothing beyond the temporary lock.
